classification.difficultyReason: Find the square's side from its diagonal, then calculate the face slant height from a lateral edge before summing face areas.

content.prompt: Calculate the surface area of this pyramid. Round your answer to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded right square pyramid with four matching double ticks on the base edges. A lateral edge is labelled 10 cm; a separate curved leader identifies the base diagonal as 10 cm. Ordinary geometry is black, with the highlighted base diagonal in standard red.
spec.mathematics: Square base diagonal 10 cm and lateral edge 10 cm. Base side sqrt(50) cm; face slant height sqrt(175/2) cm. The coordinate model uses a uniformly scaled square base and centred apex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the two supplied 10 cm measurements and equal-base-edge marks are visible; derived lengths and areas occur only in answers.

answer.worked:
Side length of the square base:
$$\begin{align*}2s^2&=10^2\\s^2&=50\\s&=\sqrt{50}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Slant height of each triangular face:
$$\begin{align*}l^2&=10^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt{50}}{2}\right)^2\\l^2&=\frac{175}{2}\\l&=\sqrt{\frac{175}{2}}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{align*}A&=(\sqrt{50})^2+4\left(\frac12\times\sqrt{50}\times\sqrt{\frac{175}{2}}\right)\\A&=50+50\sqrt7\\A&\approx182.3\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
